analysis.evidence: אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה means “after these events.” The phrase points back to what has already happened and places Abram’s vision after it.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural noun in the absolute state. The following demonstrative הָאֵלֶּה agrees with it.

analysis.evidence: In אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה, “after these events,” the demonstrative agrees with הַדְּבָרִים in number and definiteness and points back to the events just recounted.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes the common plural demonstrative אֵלֶּה, which modifies הַדְּבָרִים.

analysis.evidence: אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה places the event after the preceding events. הָיָה דְבַר יַהְוֶה אֶל אַבְרָם reports that the word of Yahweh came to Abram, and לֵאמֹר introduces what Yahweh said.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject דְבַר יַהְוֶה. The verb has no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: דְבַר יַהְוֶה identifies Yahweh as the source of the message, and אֶל אַבְרָם identifies Abram as its recipient. לֵאמֹר introduces the message itself, beginning with אַל תִּירָא אַבְרָם, “Do not fear, Abram.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with יַהְוֶה as its complement.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
